GRADE 7 MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Time: 96 minutes

INSTRUCTIONS
1. This is an advanced revision paper.
2. Show working where needed.
3. Answer all questions.
2. For multiple choice, write the correct letter only.
3. For short answers, write clearly in the spaces provided.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A: Multiple Choice

1. About Whole Numbers at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. use place value and total value of digits up to hundreds of millions in real-life
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

2. About Whole Numbers using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. read and write numbers in symbols up to hundreds of millions in real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

3. About Whole Numbers when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. read and write numbers in words up to millions for fluency
   B. Learners should ignore Whole Numbers completely.
   C. Whole Numbers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Whole Numbers.

5. About Factors at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. test divisibility of numbers by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9,10 and 11 in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Factors completely.
   C. Factors is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Factors.

6. About Factors using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. express composite numbers as a product of prime factors in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Factors completely.
   C. Factors is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Factors.

7. About Factors when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the Greatest Common Divisor (GC
   B. Learners should ignore Factors completely.
   C. Factors is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Factors.

9. About Fractions at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. compare fractions in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

10. About Fractions using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. add fractions in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

11. About Fractions when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. subtract fractions in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Fractions completely.
   C. Fractions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Fractions.

13. About Decimals at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify the place value and the total value of digits in decimals in real-life
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

14. About Decimals using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. multiply decimals by a whole number and by a decimal in real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

15. About Decimals when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. divide decimals by a whole number and by a decimal in real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Decimals completely.
   C. Decimals is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Decimals.

17. About Squares and Square Roots at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. determine the squares of whole numbers, fractions, and decimals by multiplication in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Squares and Square Roots completely.
   C. Squares and Square Roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Squares and Square Roots.

18. About Squares and Square Roots using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. determine the square roots of whole numbers, fractions, and decimals of perfect squares in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Squares and Square Roots completely.
   C. Squares and Square Roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Squares and Square Roots.

19. About Squares and Square Roots when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. determine the squares of whole numbers, fractions, and decimals by multiplication in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Squares and Square Roots completely.
   C. Squares and Square Roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Squares and Square Roots.

21. About Algebraic Expressions at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. form algebraic expressions from real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Algebraic Expressions completely.
   C. Algebraic Expressions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Algebraic Expressions.

22. About Algebraic Expressions using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. form algebraic expressions from simple algebraic statements in real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Algebraic Expressions completely.
   C. Algebraic Expressions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Algebraic Expressions.

23. About Algebraic Expressions when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. simplify algebraic expressions in real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Algebraic Expressions completely.
   C. Algebraic Expressions is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Algebraic Expressions.

25. About Linear Equations at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. form linear equations in one unknown in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Equations completely.
   C. Linear Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Equations.

26. About Linear Equations using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. solve linear equations in one unknown in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Equations completely.
   C. Linear Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Equations.

27. About Linear Equations when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. apply linear equations in one unknown to real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Equations completely.
   C. Linear Equations is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Equations.

29. About Linear Inequalities at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. apply inequality symbols to inequality statements in learning situations
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Inequalities completely.
   C. Linear Inequalities is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Inequalities.

30. About Linear Inequalities using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. form simple linear inequalities in one unknown in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Inequalities completely.
   C. Linear Inequalities is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Inequalities.

31. About Linear Inequalities when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. illustrate simple inequalities on a number line
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Inequalities completely.
   C. Linear Inequalities is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Inequalities.

33. About Pythagorean Relationship at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. recognise the sides of a right- angled triangle in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Pythagorean Relationship completely.
   C. Pythagorean Relationship is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Pythagorean Relationship.

34. About Pythagorean Relationship using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. identify Pythagorean relationships in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Pythagorean Relationship completely.
   C. Pythagorean Relationship is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Pythagorean Relationship.

35. About Pythagorean Relationship when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. apply Pythagorean relationship to real-life situations
   B. Learners should ignore Pythagorean Relationship completely.
   C. Pythagorean Relationship is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Pythagorean Relationship.

37. About Length at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. convert units of length from one form to another involving cm, dm, m, Dm, Hm in learning situations
   B. Learners should ignore Length completely.
   C. Length is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Length.

38. About Length using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. perform operations involving units of length in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Length completely.
   C. Length is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Length.

39. About Length when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the perimeter of plane figures in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Length completely.
   C. Length is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Length.

41. About Area at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify the relationship between square metre (m2 ) and hectares as units of measuring area
   B. Learners should ignore Area completely.
   C. Area is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Area.

42. About Area using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the area of a rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, and trapezium in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Area completely.
   C. Area is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Area.

43. About Area when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the area of circles in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Area completely.
   C. Area is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Area.

45. About Volume and Capacity at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. identify metre cube (m3 ) as a unit of volume in measurements
   B. Learners should ignore Volume and Capacity completely.
   C. Volume and Capacity is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Volume and Capacity.

46. About Volume and Capacity using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. convert metre cube (m3 ) into centimeter cube (cm3 ) and vice versa in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Volume and Capacity completely.
   C. Volume and Capacity is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Volume and Capacity.

47. About Volume and Capacity when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the volume of cubes, cuboids, and cylinders in different situations
   B. Learners should ignore Volume and Capacity completely.
   C. Volume and Capacity is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Volume and Capacity.
